q: What is the purpose of exploratory data analysis before building a model?
options: To profile, summarise and plot the data to understand its quality
To tune the final model settings until test accuracy stops improving
To deploy a trained model and monitor how it behaves on live data
To replace validation by checking the model against the training set
explain: EDA happens before formal modelling. It builds a picture of the data's content, quality, relationships and anomalies. Tuning, deployment and validation come later.

q: A feature correlates almost perfectly with the target. What should you suspect first?
options: Target leakage, where the feature reveals the label
A perfect predictor that should simply be kept in the model
Class imbalance in the target column
A skewed feature that needs a log transform
explain: Correlations that are too perfect are a warning of leakage. A model using the leaked feature would look good in testing but fail on real new data.

How strongly each feature can be explained by the other features
How many values in each feature are missing
How evenly the classes are spread across the dataset
explain: Multicollinearity describes how strongly a feature can be explained by the other features. The variance inflation factor measures it and helps decide which variables to drop, combine or regularise. How strongly a feature relates to the target is a different check.

q: A dataset has a rare positive class. Which responses are sensible?
options: Report overall accuracy only because it is the simplest measure
Use stratified splits so each split keeps the class mix
Use class weights or resampling
Judge the model with measures such as F1 or PR-AUC
Delete the rare class so the classes are balanced
explain: Imbalance makes accuracy misleading and can hide poor performance on the rare class. Deleting that class removes the very cases you care about.

q: Describe how missing values and outliers are investigated in tabular data and what decisions the checks inform.
model: For missing values you measure where data are missing, how much, and whether gaps occur together or relate to the outcome. This shows which columns need imputing or dropping and warns of possible bias. For outliers you use robust rules such as the interquartile range and then inspect the flagged rows. The aim is to separate data entry errors from true extremes. Errors are fixed or removed, while real extremes lead to capping, transforming or choosing a model that copes with them.
points: Missingness is measured by column, proportion and pattern
It informs imputation or dropping and flags bias
Outliers are found with robust rules and then inspected
Errors are separated from legitimate extremes before deciding what to do

q: Explain what class imbalance is, why it matters and how EDA helps you respond.
model: Class imbalance means some classes or target regions occur much less often than others. It matters because a model can score high overall accuracy by favouring the common class while missing the rare one. EDA checks the class proportions early. If imbalance is found you can use stratified splits so each set keeps the mix, choose metrics such as F1 or PR-AUC, and apply class weights or resampling.
points: Defines imbalance as unequal class frequencies
Accuracy can hide poor performance on the rare class
Checked by looking at class proportions
Responses include stratified splits, better metrics, weights or resampling

q: Explain the significance of exploratory data analysis in a machine learning project. Discuss three techniques commonly used in EDA and what each shows. What are the consequences of doing too little EDA before building a model?
model: Exploratory data analysis helps us understand the characteristics, structure and quality of a dataset before building a model. It finds patterns, relationships and problems in the data. Descriptive statistics such as mean, median, standard deviation, minimum and maximum show the distribution and spread of numerical features. Visualisation with histograms and box plots shows distributions, skewness and outliers. Correlation analysis shows relationships between numerical variables and possible multicollinearity. Too little EDA can leave missing values, outliers, wrong data types or highly correlated features undetected. These harm training, give misleading results and lower predictive performance, so EDA guides the choice of preprocessing and algorithm.
points: EDA shows the structure, quality and patterns of the data before modelling
Descriptive statistics show distribution and spread
Histograms or box plots show skewness and outliers
Correlation analysis shows relationships and multicollinearity
Too little EDA leaves missing values, outliers or wrong types that harm the model

q: Which is the most appropriate method for identifying possible outliers in a continuous numerical variable?
options: Pie chart
Box plot
Bar chart
Confusion matrix
explain: A box plot shows the spread of a numerical variable and marks points beyond the whiskers as possible outliers. Pie and bar charts suit categories, and a confusion matrix evaluates a classifier.

q: Which statement about a correlation coefficient of -0.85 is correct?
options: The variables have a strong negative linear relationship
One variable causes the other to decrease
The variables have a weak positive relationship
The relationship must be nonlinear
explain: A value near -1 means a strong negative linear relationship. Correlation does not show cause.
